item.title: Classical cumulants from the double tensor unshuffle Hopf algebra
item.description: arXiv:2610.33382v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We realize classical cumulants and their fixed-point equations in the double tensor unshuffle Hopf algebra introduced by Ebrahimi-Fard and Patras, placing classical, free, Boolean, and monotone cumulants in a common algebraic framework. A concatenation perturbation of the functionals yields left and right half-shuffle equations on ordinary words without changing the coproduct or either half-coproduct. Both equations are equivalent to the classical moment--cumulant formula and uniquely determine the classical cumulants. We also obtain a Hopf-algebraic realization of the classical-to-free cumulant transform through convolution exponentiation and the left half-shuffle logarithm. A commutative diagram identifies its partition-level action with summation over non-crossing closure fibers, recovering Lehner's closure-fiber formula within the framework of the double tensor unshuffle Hopf algebra.
item.dc:creator: Xing Gao, Jingtao Li

item.title: Remarks on covariant differential calculus on the non-standard quantum Podle\'s sphere
item.description: arXiv:2610.33572v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An $SU_q(2)$-covariant first-order differential calculus on the non-standard quantum Podle\'s two-sphere is constructed. The module of one-forms is explicitly given in terms of modules of sections of charge $\pm 2$ line bundles associated to the quantum Hopf fibration.
item.dc:creator: Tomasz Brzezinski, R\'eamonn \'O Buachalla

item.title: Crossed modularity of twisted VOA modules
item.description: arXiv:2610.34193v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $V$ be a strongly rational vertex operator algebra and $G\leq\operatorname{Aut}(V)$ a finite group. Using the $G$-crossed braided fusion structure of twisted modules constructed in \cite{Crossed}, we prove that the conformal twist $e^{2\pi iL(0)}$ gives a crossed ribbon structure and that the crossed category is modular in Kirillov's sense. Consequently, its equivariantization is a modular tensor category. We also obtain dimension and simple-object counting formulas for the twisted sectors.
item.dc:creator: Shun Xu

item.title: Automatic cocommutativity for the quantum-group comonad
item.description: arXiv:2610.34332v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the cofree Hopf algebra on a cocommutative bialgebra is again cocommutative, and in fact coincides with the latter's largest Hopf subalgebra. This answers a question of Ardizzoni-Menini-Saracco and provides a proof for a statement to the same effect in the literature, whose original justification contains an apparent gap. The result relies on (and is in fact equivalent to) the observation that cocommutative bialgebra quotients of arbitrary Hopf algebras are automatically Hopf. This latter statement strengthens the analogue due to Newman, which assumes cocommutativity for the Hopf domain. One application of the above is the following quantum-rigidity result for Hopf algebras acted upon by a covariant quantum group: an action by one Hopf algebra on another which preserves the unital-algebra structure and the comultiplication factors through an action by a cocommutative Hopf algebra which moreover preserves the entire Hopf structure.
item.dc:creator: Alexandru Chirvasitu

item.title: Faithful Localization of Vertex Algebra Modules
item.description: arXiv:2610.34953v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a Faithfulness Theorem for vertex algebra modules, showing that two complementary geometric localizations can jointly detect global algebraic structure. We apply this principle to vertex algebras obtained by BRST reduction from classical invariant theory and identify them, under natural geometric hypotheses, with global sections of sheaves of chiral differential operators. As consequences, we prove vanishing of BRST cohomology in nonzero degrees and simplicity, and show that every finitely strongly generated module is a finite direct sum of copies of the vacuum module. In particular, the corresponding module category is equivalent to the category of finite-dimensional vector spaces. For families associated with classical groups, we identify the associated varieties with Hamiltonian reductions, proving quasi-lisse-ness and the predicted identification with Higgs branches of the corresponding supersymmetric gauge theories. This provides geometric realizations of a broad class of vertex algebras arising from three- and four-dimensional quantum field theories.
item.dc:creator: Tomoyuki Arakawa, Xuanzhong Dai, Bailin Song

item.title: Duflo--Serganova functor for chiral differential operators on classical invariant rings
item.description: arXiv:2610.34954v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Duflo--Serganova functor for vertex algebras of chiral differential operators on classical invariant rings, introduced in \cite{ADS}. Our main result is a general cancellation theorem showing that a common bosonic and fermionic summand can be removed by Duflo--Serganova reduction. We apply this theorem to obtain Duflo--Serganova reduction isomorphisms for two families of simple orthosymplectic affine vertex superalgebras at levels $-2n$ and $n$, which are not covered by the existing results of Gorelik and Serganova. As a consequence, we obtain supercharacter identities, including the conjecture of Adamovi\'c and Milas as a special case.
item.dc:creator: Tomoyuki Arakawa, Xuanzhong Dai, Bailin Song

item.title: Pentagon Equation in Deformation Quantization of Character Varieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.35446v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deformation quantizations of the moduli space of framed flat bundles live naturally in the Drinfeld category. Such quantizations were constructed using the so-called quantum fusion by Li-Bland and \v{S}evera. We give a complete characterization of the dependence of this quantization on combinatorial choices, and prove that these quantizations are all isomorphic, forming vertices of an explicitly constructed complete commuting graph of algebra isomorphism. To this end, we extend the Kontsevich integral methods of Le and Murakami from even associators to all associators. Finally, we also prove that bi-invariant Haar measures provide traces on these quantizations.
item.dc:creator: J\'an Pulmann

item.title: On generators and relations for $O_n^\circ(V)$ in higher-level Zhu algebras, Part II
item.description: arXiv:2610.35527v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study circle relations in the higher-level Zhu algebra of a vertex operator algebra $V$. For regular vacuum words in homogeneous letters, we prove the termwise correction-residue conjecture of Part I: every correction in the one-sided iterate expansion belongs separately to the finite-length plus subspace. The first correction formed with the left truncated field vanishes identically. Multiplying the diagonal commutator kernel by a power of $1+x$ turns it into a Laurent polynomial. This proves the vanishing and writes every other correction as a finite combination of product residues with fewer $Y_L$ factors, coming from the word obtained by replacing one negative mode by a nonnegative one. These results hold at all levels $n\ge0$, without an auxiliary-degree hypothesis. For $n\ge1$ and a homogeneous ordered pair $(u,v)$, two explicit triangular families span the quadratic residue operators modulo the length-one and singular-iterate relations, giving $\dim\mathcal{Q}_n((u,v))\le n(n+1)$. The universal product-coefficient arrays have dimension exactly $n(n+1)$ and three natural bases; restriction to the regular mode square is an isomorphism. This proves operator spanning and gives invertible matrices for two complementary diagonal eliminations. For equal inputs, mode interchange reduces the families to their odd-indexed members, giving $\dim\mathcal{Q}_n((u,u))\le 2\lfloor (n+1)^2/4\rfloor$. The pairwise estimates give an explicit global quadratic bound for any finite homogeneous strong generating set. Heisenberg, Virasoro, and affine $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ examples illustrate equality and strict inequality in the operator bounds.
item.dc:creator: Nathan P Vander Werf

item.title: Grothendieck rings of near-Tambara--Yamagami fusion categories
item.description: arXiv:2610.35574v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the Grothendieck rings of fusion categories over $\mathcal{C}$ containing a nonpointed Tambara--Yamagami fusion subcategory and exactly one further simple object. The subcategory necessarily has rank five, its invertible objects form the Klein four-group, and the coefficient $\kappa$ of the additional simple object in its tensor square belongs to $\{0,2,7\}$. Each of these three based rings is categorifiable. For $\kappa=0$, every category belongs, up to tensor equivalence, to the rank-one odd-component extension list of Choi--Lu--Sun. For $\kappa=2$ we construct an explicit unitary group-theoretical realization, and for $\kappa=7$ a realization is $\rm{Rep}(\rm{PSU}(3,2))$.
item.dc:creator: Jingcheng Dong, S\'ebastien Palcoux, Kai Wang

item.title: Heavy Heisenberg Algebras, Zero Modes and Modularity
item.description: arXiv:2610.35749v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It is known due to a result of Miyamoto that zero mode correlators of weight $1$ vectors of vertex operator algebras are quasi-modular forms, and that their generating series are Jacobi forms. In this article we generalize this to higher weight vectors. We consider weight 2 vectors that generate what we call heavy Heisenberg algebras. We prove that their zero mode correlators are a specific type of quasi-modular forms. As a consequence, they too can be summed up into a generating series with Jacobi-like modular transformation properties. As an application of our results, we sketch an argument that gives the asymptotic behavior of the dimensions of states of our VOAs.
item.dc:creator: Darlayne Addabbo, Christoph A. Keller

item.title: Construction of holomorphic SCFTs with minimal index
item.description: arXiv:2610.33165v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: It has been an open question whether there exist holomorphic VOAs with N=1 supersymmetry and Witten index 1 for any positive central charge c. The existence of such a theory with c=288 is closely related to the 576-periodicity of the TMF spectrum via the Segal-Stolz-Teichner conjecture. Here we report the construction of thousands of such theories by extending the approach initiated by Gaiotto and Johnson-Freyd via ternary codes. In addition, for every positive integer k, we also construct holomorphic N=1 VOAs of central charge c=12k with index 24/gcd(24,k) -- conjectured to be the minimum -- in a computer-aided search carried out by AI coding agents. We overcome the exponential-time barrier by using chains of smaller cells to build ternary codes, whose indices can then be evaluated via a transfer-matrix technique, and we use a symmetric orbifold construction to reduce the problem of k=12 and 24 to that of k=6. Along the way, we also establish several results on ternary codes and their indices. Using an observation relating codes and Landau-Ginzburg orbifold models, we argue that the non-chiral doubles of the ternary code VOAs can always be gapped supersymmetrically.
item.dc:creator: Du Pei

item.title: Extensions of a family of Linear Cycle Sets whose underlying group is a product of two cyclic groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.33192v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We use the linear cycle set cohomology in order to compute extensions of a non trivial linear cycle sets whose underlying additive group is a product of two cyclic groups.
item.dc:creator: Jorge Guccione, Juan Jos\'e Guccione, Christian Valqui

item.title: A note on Rota-Baxter affgebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.33573v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: An affinization of a concept of a Rota-Baxter operator or Rota-Baxter affgebras are discussed. Rota-Baxter Lie affgebras and their relation to Rota-Baxter Lie algebras are treated in more detail. In particular it is shown that every Rota-Baxter Lie affgebra is isomorphic to a Rota-Baxter Lie affgebra with a Lie algebra fibre over which the affine Rota-Baxter operator is linear.
item.dc:creator: Tomasz Brzezi\'nski

item.title: Matrix representations of ${\rm BC}_n$ associative Yang--Baxter equations and related long-range spin chains
item.description: arXiv:2610.33913v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct a matrix representation of the algebra defined by the associative Yang--Baxter equations of ${\rm BC}_n$ type. In the elliptic case, two sets of generators are represented in terms of the Baxter--Belavin quantum $R$-matrix in the fundamental representation of ${\rm GL}_N$, while the remaining generators are represented by the elliptic $K$-matrix found by Komori and Hikami. We revisit its derivation using the Felder--Pasquier procedure and correct the unitarity relation for odd $N$. We then use these matrix representations to construct examples of long-range quantum spin chains from $R$-matrix-valued Lax pairs for the classical Calogero--Inozemtsev system associated with the ${\rm BC}_n$ root system. We also construct $R$-matrix-valued Lax pairs for Calogero--Moser models in an external field, leading to Haldane--Shastry and Polychronakos--Frahm chains with modified spin positions.
item.dc:creator: M. Matushko, A. Mostovskii, A. Zotov

item.title: Exponentially large mu-coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2610.34982v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Using webs, we prove that Kazhdan-Lusztig mu-coefficients for symmetric groups grow at least exponentially with the rank, already for pairs labeled by a three-row rectangle.
item.dc:creator: Tom Goertzen, Abel Lacabanne, Daniel Tubbenhauer, Pedro Vaz

item.title: Convex orders in root systems and quantum tangent spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.35091v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We classify the reduced decompositions of the longest element $w_0$ of the Weyl group of a semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ for which the corresponding Lusztig quantum root vectors span a quantum tangent space in $U_q(\mathfrak{g})$. We introduce a combinatorial condition on the convex order induced by a reduced decomposition, tangency, and prove that a reduced decomposition gives rise to a quantum tangent space if and only if it is tangent. The proof relies on a description of the coproduct of quantum root vectors in terms of the convex order, and on a projection in the right weak order attached to each positive root. Up to commutation, tangent reduced decompositions are obtained by concatenating the longest minimal coset representatives along a chain of cominuscule parabolic quotients; in particular there are none in types $E_8$, $F_4$ and $G_2$.
item.dc:creator: Alessandro Carotenuto, Christophe Hohlweg, Paolo Papi

item.title: The counts of parity-odd vs even late-growing permutations in the group $\mathbb{S}_{2p-1}$ differ by $(-1)^p$
item.description: arXiv:2610.35779v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A permutation $\sigma\in\mathbb{S}_n$ of objects $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ is called \emph{late-growing} if its partial sums never exceed the respective partial sums of the `average' permutation (with the arithmetic mean $n^{-1}\cdot\sum_{i=1}^n i = (n+1)/2$ of $1,\ldots,n$ on average at each entry $\sigma(i)$): $\sum_{i=1}^k \sigma(i) \leqslant k\cdot (n+1)/2$ for all positive $k\leqslant n$. We prove that for $n=2p-1$ odd, the set $\Phi_p\subseteq \mathbb{S}_{2p-1}$ of late-growing permutations is partitioned into parity-even vs odd elements, $\Phi_p = \Phi_p^{+} \sqcup \Phi_p^{-}$, in an almost symmetric way: $| \Phi_p^{+} | - | \Phi_p^{-} | = (-1)^{p+1}$. The proof is constructive: by viewing the permutations $\sigma\in\Phi_p$ as constrained walks on the integral lattice $\mathbb{Z}$, we describe two filters that pair all but one element in $\Phi_p^{+}$ versus $\Phi_p^{-}$; the remaining walk $\sigma^*$ with monotonically growing step amplitudes determines the dominant parity subset.
item.dc:creator: Kian C. Shah, Arthemy V. Kiselev

item.title: Algorithm for computing canonical bases and foldings of quantum groups
item.description: arXiv:2506.00793v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let ${\mathbf U}_q^-$ be the negative half of a quantum group of finite type. Let $P$ be the transition matrix between the canonical basis and a PBW basis of ${\mathbf U}_q^-$. In the case ${\mathbf U}_q^-$ is symmetric, Antor gave a simple algorithm of computing $P$ by making use of monomial bases. By the folding theory, ${\mathbf U}_q^-$ (symmetric, with a certain automorphism) is related to a quantum group $\underline{{\mathbf U}}_q^-$ of non-symmetric type. In this paper, we extend the results of Antor to the non-symmetric case, and discuss the relationship between the algorithms for ${\mathbf U}_q^-$ and for $\underline{\mathbf U}_q^-$.
item.dc:creator: Toshiaki Shoji, Zhiping Zhou

item.title: Nijenhuis pre-Lie bialgebras, Nijenhuis Lie bialgebras and \sss-equation
item.description: arXiv:2508.02983v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a bialgebraic framework for Nijenhuis operators on pre-Lie algebras and coalgebras. Starting from dual triangular pre-Lie bialgebras and weak pseudo-Hessian structures, we construct Nijenhuis operators on pre-Lie algebras and establish the corresponding coalgebraic construction. We introduce Nijenhuis pre-Lie bialgebras, characterize them through matched pairs, and identify compatibility conditions linking the two constructions. For triangular structures, we formulate the $S$-Nijenhuis $\mathbb{S}$-equation, give an operator characterization, and obtain constructions using relative Rota-Baxter operators. We also show that balanced Nijenhuis pre-Lie bialgebras give rise to Nijenhuis Lie bialgebras. Finally, we introduce crossed modules and braided Nijenhuis pre-Lie bialgebras, and characterize when compatible algebraic and coalgebraic data assemble into a Nijenhuis pre-Lie biproduct. These results connect Nijenhuis operators with pre-Lie bialgebra structures, Yang-Baxter-type equations, and constructions on representations.
item.dc:creator: Li Guo, Tianshui Ma

item.title: Freidel-Maillet type equations on fused K-matrices over the positive part of $U_q(\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}_2)$
item.description: arXiv:2512.00819v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The positive part $U_q^+$ of the quantized enveloping algebra $U_q(\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}_2)$ has a reflection equation presentation of Freidel-Maillet type (Baseilhac 2022). Its defining K-matrix has size $2 \times 2$ and can be expressed, using Rosso's embedding of $U_q^+$ into a $q$-shuffle algebra, as generating functions whose coefficients are Terwilliger's alternating PBW basis elements. This and older PBW bases of $U_q^+$ due to Damiani and Beck are unified by linear combinations of Catalan words (Ruan 2025). In this paper, we use this unification to define K-operators of any dimension $\geq 2$ in matrix form; the entries are explicit generating functions over $U_q^+$. Our main result is that any pair of such K-matrices, possibly of different dimensions, satisfy a Freidel-Maillet type equation. This yields a family of algebraic relations over $U_q^+$ that generalize Baseilhac's equation and can be used to study integrable systems or higher-spin representations. We conjecture that, for every spin, these K-matrices coincide with Lusztig's quasi R-matrix evaluated with its first leg on the corresponding finite-dimensional irreducible module.
item.dc:creator: Chenwei Ruan

item.title: Twisted Yangians of split types BI, CI, DI and Drinfeld type current relations
item.description: arXiv:2607.14692v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study twisted Yangians associated with the split symmetric pairs of types BI, CI and DI. We introduce a new presentation of these algebras, which we call the transposed presentation, governed by a twisted reflection equation that interacts naturally with the Gaussian decomposition of the generating matrix. Working entirely within the $R$-matrix presentation, we derive Drinfeld-type current presentations of the special twisted Yangian $SY^{\mathrm{tw}}(\mathfrak{g}_N)$ and of the extended twisted Yangian $X^{\mathrm{tw}}(\mathfrak{g}_N)$, in which the Serre relations are stated in a closed current form. Extracting coefficients recovers the Drinfeld presentation of Lu, Wang and Zhang, in the normalisation of Lu. As a consequence, we establish an explicit isomorphism between the $R$-matrix and Drinfeld presentations conjectured by Lu, Wang and Zhang. As a byproduct, we obtain a tensor product decomposition of $X^{\mathrm{tw}}(\mathfrak{g}_N)$ into the twisted Yangian in the Drinfeld presentation and a polynomial ring in countably many central variables. We also obtain Poincar\'e-Birkhoff-Witt bases in the Drinfeld generators and the coideal coproduct on the low Drinfeld modes at all but the last node.
item.dc:creator: Vidas Regelskis

item.title: A note on the center of the queer super Yangian ${\rm Y}(\mathfrak{q}_1)$
item.description: arXiv:2608.30293v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate two families of central elements of the queer super Yangian ${\rm Y}(\mathfrak{q}_1)$, arising from the constructions of Poletaeva-Serganova and from Nazarov's quantum Berezinian. We establish an explicit relation between their generating series, thereby giving an answer to the question raised by Nazarov in \cite{Na22}.
item.dc:creator: Hao Chang, Hongmei Hu

item.title: $\delta$-derivations of n-ary algebras
item.description: arXiv:1107.4427v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We give a description of $\delta$-derivations of $(n+1)$-dimensional $n$-ary Filippov algebras and, as a consequence, of simple finite-dimensional Filippov algebras over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. We also give new examples of non-trivial $\delta$-derivations of Filippov algebras and show that there are no non-trivial $\delta$-derivations of the simple ternary Malcev algebra $M_8$.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: I. Kaygorodov, On $\delta$-derivations of n-ary algebras, Izv. Math. 76 (2012), no. 6, 1150-1162
item.dc:creator: Ivan Kaygorodov

item.title: From Cherednik algebras to knot homology via cuspidal D-modules
item.description: arXiv:2407.00971v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove a rational generalization of Haiman's master formula, conjectured by Gorsky and Negu\c{t}: the bigraded Frobenius character of the associated graded of the finite-dimensional representation $L_{m/n}$ of the rational Cherednik algebra at slope $m/n$ can be expressed using the generator of the same slope in the elliptic Hall algebra acting on its polynomial representation. The filtration on $L_{m/n}$ is induced by the Hodge filtration on the cuspidal character $D$-module. As a corollary, we relate the triply-graded Khovanov-Rozansky homology of the torus knot to the sum of hook multiplicity spaces of $L_{m/n}$, proving a conjecture of Gorsky, Oblomkov, Rasmussen and Shende. We further provide a realization of the torus knot homology in terms of explicit coherent sheaves on Hilbert schemes of points in the plane.
item.dc:creator: Xinchun Ma

item.title: Anyonic membranes and Pontryagin statistics
item.description: arXiv:2509.14314v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Anyons, unique to two spatial dimensions, underlie extraordinary phenomena such as the fractional quantum Hall effect, but their generalization to higher dimensions has remained elusive. The topology of Eilenberg-MacLane spaces constrains the loop statistics to be only bosonic or fermionic in any dimension. In this work, we introduce the novel anyonic statistics for membrane excitations in four dimensions. Analogous to the $\mathbb{Z}_N$-particle exhibiting $\mathbb{Z}_{N\times \gcd(2,N)}$ anyonic statistics in two dimensions, we show that the $\mathbb{Z}_N$-membrane possesses $\mathbb{Z}_{N\times \gcd(3,N)}$ anyonic statistics in four dimensions. Given unitary volume operators that create membrane excitations on the boundary, we propose an explicit 56-step unitary sequence that detects the membrane statistics. We further analyze the boundary theory of $(5{+}1)$D 1-form $\mathbb{Z}_N$ symmetry-protected topological phases and demonstrate that their domain walls realize all possible anyonic membrane statistics. We then show that the $\mathbb{Z}_3$ subgroup persists in all higher dimensions. In addition to the standard fermionic $\mathbb{Z}_2$ membrane statistics arising from Stiefel-Whitney classes, membranes also exhibit $\mathbb{Z}_3$ statistics associated with Pontryagin classes. We explicitly verify that the 56-step process detects the nontrivial $\mathbb{Z}_3$ statistics in 5, 6, and 7 spatial dimensions. Moreover, in 7 and higher dimensions, the statistics of membrane excitations stabilize to $\mathbb{Z}_{2} \times \mathbb{Z}_{3}$, with the $\mathbb{Z}_3$ sector consistently captured by this process.
item.dc:creator: Yitao Feng, Hanyu Xue, Yuyang Li, Meng Cheng, Ryohei Kobayashi, Po-Shen Hsin, Yu-An Chen

item.title: On dualizability and invertibility in the higher Morita category
item.description: arXiv:2607.16953v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove a conjecture of Lurie characterizing $(n+1)$-dualizability in higher Morita categories of $\mathbb{E}_n$-algebras in terms of dualizability over certain factorization homologies. A key ingredient is a higher Morita category based on the recently developed framework of pointless factorization algebras of Karlsson and the first author. We also verify an invertibility conjecture of Brochier--Jordan--Safranov--Snyder as an immediate corollary of our main result. Moreover, we prove a relative version of the dualizability conjecture, yielding a new criterion for relative/twisted field theories. We give some examples, including Dirichlet and Neumann relative theories.
item.dc:creator: Claudia Scheimbauer, Pelle Steffens, William Stewart

item.title: Dynamical Lie Algebras for Fixed-Gate Quantum Ans\"atze
item.description: arXiv:2610.13709v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Parameterized Quantum Circuits have emerged as a central framework for variational quantum algorithms in the NISQ regime, with major applications in quantum simulation, combinatorial optimization, and, more recently, quantum machine learning (QML). By developing a new approach for computing dynamical Lie algebras associated with quantum circuits combining parametrized gates and non-parametrized entangling gates, we aim to extend the applicability of recent algebraic results to architectures that are actually used in quantum machine learning.
item.dc:creator: Orlane Zang, Daniel Juteau, Tony Quertier, Gr\'egoire Barru\'e

item.title: Plabic promotions beyond cluster: quantum cluster structures and the dual canonical basis
item.description: arXiv:2610.31655v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Plabic tangles define geometric promotion maps between configurations and, after choosing a lift, between Grassmannians. The main conjecture in \cite{Tangles} is that when the tangle is dominant and solvable the induced algebraic promotion is cluster quasi-homomorphism. This work extends the cluster perspective in two directions. First, we initiate the study of quantum promotions. We conjecture that all promotions defined from dominant solvable tangles are naturally lifted to a \emph{quantum cluster quasi homomorphism}, and prove for all cases in the literature that the were shown to be (classical) cluster quasi-homomorphisms. Secondly, we define the notion of cluster-Lusztig quasi-homomorphisms, which are cluster quasi homomorphisms that take Lustig's dual canonical basis elements to dual canonical basis element, up to a Laurent monomial in frozen variables, with clearing and normalization chosen uniformly on each content component. We prove the unexpected result that the classical and quantum $m$-unary star promotions fall into this category, and conjecture that all promotions coming from dominant solvable tangles share the same property. We then consider promotions via non solvable cores of intersection number higher than one. We use it to study facets of amplituhedron cells, and to show that some of them do not lie in zero loci of dual canonical basis elements, disproving a conjecture by T. Lam \cite{LamGP}.
item.dc:creator: Jian-Rong Li, Michael Oren Perlstein, Ran J. Tessler
